paper.title: Stochastic Linear Optimization with Adversarial Corruption

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear optimization with adversarial corruption
unmapped: corruption functions c_t: D -> [-1,1] chosen per round; corruption budget C unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote:
Let $\xSet \subseteq eals^\dimension$ be a $\dimension$-polytope. ... reward as $eward_t(\context_t) = \inner{\context_t}{\hidden} + 
oise_t$ ... sub-Gaussian random noise with mean 0 and variance proxy 1 ... $
orm{\hidden}_2 \leq 1$ and $
orm{\context}_2 \leq 1$ ... there is an adaptive adversary who may corrupt the observed reward by choosing a corruption function $\corruptionf_t:\xSet 	o [-1, 1]$ ... The value of $\corruption$ is unknown to the algorithm, which is, in turn, evaluated by pseudo-regret

conditions: exact Lowner-John ellipsoid of D used for the exploration set
tuning: zeta = 2^14 d^5 log(4 d log T / delta) (as in proof)

source.label: thm:final regret
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\confidence$, the regret is bounded by \regret = \bigO{\frac{\dimension^{2} \corruption \log \horizon}{\truediff} + \frac{\dimension^5 \log (\sfrac{\dimension \log \horizon}{\delta})\log \horizon}{\truediff^2}}.

results.notes: Regret is pseudo-regret sum <x*-x_t, theta> bounded w.p. 1-delta. Delta is gap between best and second-best extreme points (Delta_lin). Algorithm box sets zeta with d^6 while the proof uses d^5; the d^5 version corresponds to exact John ellipsoid. Computation of exact John ellipsoid not claimed polynomial.

tuning: zeta = 2^14 d^6 log(4 d log T / delta)
weak Lowner-John ellipsoid computed in polynomial time (Lovasz)

source.quote: By plugging the polynomial time algorithm for finding John's ellipsoid from \citet{lovasz1990geometric} into our \Cref{alg:explobycoor}, and setting the parameter $\parameter = 2^{14} \dimension^6 \log (\sfrac{4\dimension \log \horizon}{\delta})$, we have an computationally efficient algorithm whose regret is of $\bigO{\frac{\dimension^{5/2} \corruption \log \horizon}{\truediff} + \frac{\dimension^6 \log (\sfrac{\dimension \log \horizon}{\delta}) \log \horizon}{\truediff^2}}$.

results.notes: Stated in text, not a formal theorem; high-probability (w.p. 1-delta) per conclusion. Conclusion also states expected regret O(d^{5/2} C log T/Delta + d^6 log^2 T/Delta^2) with delta=1/T (not recorded separately).
